purpose: Token-cost and break-even feasibility analysis for extending the current rule-based ABM into hybrid/full LLM multi-agent simulation.

pricing_sources.source_note: Official OpenAI model page reports text token prices per 1M tokens. Recheck before final thesis experiments.
Official OpenAI model page reports text token prices per 1M tokens. Recheck before final thesis experiments.
Groq public pricing page lists Llama 3.1 8B Instant at $0.05 input and $0.08 output per 1M tokens. Free quota/rate limits may apply.
Groq public pricing page lists Llama 3.3 70B Versatile at $0.59 input and $0.79 output per 1M tokens. Free quota/rate limits may apply.

architectures.name: rule_based_abm
architectures.description: Current baseline: agents follow rules/probabilistic behavior. No LLM call.

architectures.name: hybrid_policy_only
architectures.description: Only a policy-maker LLM summarizes simulation outcomes and selects/justifies policy.

architectures.name: hybrid_analyst_policy
architectures.description: Rule-based customer/fraud/system agents; LLM analyst and LLM policy-maker interpret cases and policy trade-offs.

architectures.name: full_llm_abm
architectures.description: Several agents use LLM reasoning, including customer, risky actor, analyst, system narrative, and policy-maker agents.

decision_rule.technical_feasibility: Cost per scenario and latency should remain small enough to run repeated scenario tests.
decision_rule.economic_feasibility: LLM simulation is feasible only if improvement in policy net benefit exceeds token cost and latency is acceptable.
decision_rule.recommended_next_step: Run an empirical API/LangSmith pilot and replace estimated tokens/latency with measured usage.
